title: Ransomware readiness
heading:
How ready are you for
ransomware?
lead: Eight quick questions across the controls that actually stop and contain ransomware show where you are exposed and what to fix first.

items.name: Backups
items.q: Do you have backups that ransomware cannot reach or encrypt?
opts: Backups exist but are online and untested.
Tested backups with an offline or immutable copy kept separate.

items.name: MFA on entry points
items.q: Is MFA enforced on email and remote access?
opts: Phishing-resistant MFA on every internet-facing service.

items.name: Patching
items.q: How quickly are internet-facing systems patched?
opts: Within 48 hours, with scanning to confirm.

items.name: Endpoint detection
items.q: What would detect ransomware behaviour on a device?
opts: Managed EDR with 24/7 monitoring and response.

items.name: Email & macro controls
items.q: Is the email and macro delivery path locked down?
opts: Layered filtering, macros blocked or signed, and link protection.

items.name: Network segmentation
items.q: Would an infected device be contained, or could it spread?
opts: Flat network, it would spread freely.
Zone-based segmentation that contains lateral movement.

items.name: Privileged access
items.q: How well are administrative rights controlled?
opts: Admin rights limited and kept off email and the web.

items.name: Incident response
items.q: Do you have a tested plan for a ransomware event?
opts: A tested plan with roles, contacts, and recovery runbooks.
